paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: the LORD is worth trusting, and the proof is that His loving devotion "endures forever." The psalm opens and closes with that exact line, and it calls every nation and every people to praise Him (Psalm 117:1-2; Psalm 118:1, 29). The psalm writer wasn't singing from a comfy chair, either. He got surrounded and pushed so hard he was falling, and he says "the LORD helped me" (Psalm 118:10-13).

So when you're backed into a corner, take refuge in the LORD instead of leaning on people. The psalm says, "It is better to take refuge in the LORD than to trust in man" (Psalm 118:8). I trusted a lot of people to pull me out of a junk drawer, and friend, the only One who showed up was the LORD. Even the discipline the psalm writer felt didn't end with him given over to death, and he lives to "proclaim what the LORD has done" (Psalm 118:17-18).

Then comes the cornerstone: "The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone" (Psalm 118:22). Jesus quotes it (Matthew 21:42), and Peter, His disciple, says Jesus is that stone (Acts 4:10-11). Being turned away by people is not the end of the story when the LORD is the One building. So today, rejoice, because "This is the day that the LORD has made," and give thanks to the One who is good (Psalm 118:24, 29).
